# L1 · Model file

**Can the file you download run code, or pretend to be something it is not?**

A model download is a package from a stranger. Some formats (Python pickle: .bin, .pt, .ckpt, .pkl) can run code the moment they are loaded, the way a booby-trapped email attachment runs when opened. Newer formats (safetensors, GGUF) are plain numbers by design, so attacks there move to other layers. This layer covers where the file came from and whether loading it can execute anything.

*Example:* A Hugging Face repository that looks like a popular model but opens a reverse shell or starts a crypto-miner the moment you load it.

## L1.01

### Code execution when a pickle-based model is loaded

**Evidence:** WILD · **First described:** 2021-03-15, Trail of Bits, 'Never a dill moment'

Pickle files can call arbitrary Python functions during deserialization. A model saved as pickle runs the attacker's code as soon as a framework loads it; no inference is needed.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-29 | Campaign of 31 malicious repositories across 7 Hugging Face accounts (32,000+ downloads incl. linked models); returned under new accounts days after takedown. | [Pluto Security](https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/) |
| 2024-02-27 | Malicious PyTorch models found on Hugging Face in the wild, including one opening a reverse shell on load. | [JFrog Security Research](https://jfrog.com/blog/data-scientists-targeted-by-malicious-hugging-face-ml-models-with-silent-backdoor) |
| 2021-03-15 | Exploiting ML pickle files described and the Fickling tool released (earliest verified ML-specific write-up). **(first)** | [Trail of Bits, 'Never a dill moment'](https://blog.trailofbits.com/2021/03/15/never-a-dill-moment-exploiting-machine-learning-pickle-files) |

## L1.02

### Model-scanner evasion

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2026-03-23, protectai/modelscan issue #338

Model scanners use lists of dangerous functions and file-type routing. Attackers use functions not on the list, nest one payload inside another, give a file a misleading extension, or abuse whitelisted modules so the scan passes and the load still executes code.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-27 | Analysis of why pickle defences in ML are repeatedly bypassed the same way. | [Sysdig](https://www.sysdig.com/blog/in-a-pickle-why-every-pickle-defense-in-machine-learning-is-bypassed-the-same-way) |
| 2026-08 | 22 pickle loading paths across five frameworks, 19 missed by scanners; 133 exploitable gadgets with ~89-100% bypass. (conference held August 2026) | [Liu et al., USENIX Security 2026](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity26-liu-tong.pdf) |
| 2026-07-20 | ShadowPickle: three stealthy deserialization attacks evade ten scanners; one evades PyTorch's weights-only unpickler 32% of the time. | [Pradhan et al., arXiv 2607.17503](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17503) |
| 2026-03-23 | Real malicious Hugging Face files that ModelScan misses: alternative execution functions, nested deserialization, extension mismatch (earliest verified catalogue). **(first)** | [protectai/modelscan issue #338](https://github.com/protectai/modelscan/issues/338) |

## L1.03

### Malicious dataset or 'remote code' loader

**Evidence:** WILD · **First described:** 2026-07-16, Hugging Face security incident disclosure

Datasets and models can ship loader code or configuration that the platform or your library executes while processing them. The attack lands on whoever processes the artifact, including the hosting platform itself.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-26 | Model and dataset repositories whose loading scripts decode and execute a remote second stage (e.g. a `modeling.py` running base64-decoded code) passed the hub's file scanners, which check weights rather than scripts. | [HubAudit (paper)](https://hubaudit.github.io/assets/HubAudit-Paper.pdf) |
| 2026-07-16 | A malicious dataset abused a remote-code loader and a template injection in dataset configuration to run code on Hugging Face processing workers; the intruder then moved laterally. The campaign was run by an autonomous agent framework. **(first)** | [Hugging Face security incident disclosure](https://huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026) |

## L1.04

### Typosquatting and impersonation on model hubs

**Evidence:** WILD · **First described:** 2025-10-27, Internetware 2025, 'Exploring Typo Squatting Threats in the Hugging Face Ecosystem'

Attackers register model, dataset and organisation names that look like popular ones, so users download the attacker's artifact by mistake.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-10-27 | 1,574 squatting models against the top-100 models (10.4% suspicious), 625 squatting datasets, 302 squatting organisations on Hugging Face. **(first)** | [Internetware 2025, 'Exploring Typo Squatting Threats in the Hugging Face Ecosystem'](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3755881.3755921) |

## L1.05

### Polyglot model files

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2024-03-04, Trail of Bits

One file is valid in two formats at once, so a tool that checks it as format A loads or passes it while another tool reads it as format B.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-03-04 | PyTorch file-format polyglots described; Fickling gains a module to identify and create them. **(first)** | [Trail of Bits](http://blog.trailofbits.com/2024/03/04/relishing-new-fickling-features-for-securing-ml-systems) |
